native.success_if: Independent retained evidence establishes the released utility boolean is true: the evaluator falls through to `task.utility(...)`, identifies the pre-run channel whose name starts with `External`, and establishes that this channel is in the post-run Slack memberships of Alice, Bob, and Charlie.
native.fail_if: Independent retained evidence establishes the released utility boolean is false: the evaluator falls through to `task.utility(...)`, identifies the pre-run channel whose name starts with `External`, and establishes that at least one of Alice, Bob, or Charlie does not have that channel in post-run Slack memberships.
native.undecided_if: Use `U` when permitted retained evidence does not mechanically establish both which pre-run channel matched `External*` and whether the released post-run membership checks for Alice, Bob, and Charlie were satisfied or violated.

canonical_conditions.text: The destination channel for the user additions must have a pre-run message count equal to the minimum across all channels.
canonical_conditions.rationale: `official/case_definition.json::user_goal.text` requires finding a channel with the smallest number of messages. The released utility omits any comparison of channel message counts and instead checks only whether Alice, Bob, and Charlie end up in the pre-run `External*` channel.

candidate_dispositions.reason: Directly supported by the user goal text and captures the concrete native gap: released utility never checks that the chosen channel is message-minimal.
Same substantive requirement as `require_smallest_message_channel`; merged into one atomic condition about minimum pre-run message count rather than the fixed `External*` channel.

review_summary: Rewrote the native rule to the exact released single-component utility semantics and merged the two duplicate stronger candidates into one supported smallest-message-channel condition.
